page: Vultr vcg-a40-6c-30g-12vram is a virtual machine within the Cloud GPU family, featuring an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor. The instance is configured with 6 shared vCPUs and 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 5.0 GB per vCPU. For storage, the server includes 550 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The primary accelerator for this instance is a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, representing a 0.25 slice of the physical GPU. This allocation provides 12 GB of dedicated VRAM. Because the CPU resources are shared and the GPU is partitioned, this server offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the overhead of a full dedicated card. However, the shared CPU allocation means performance may vary depending on host node neighbor activity.

This hardware profile is suited for workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration but do not require a full dedicated GPU or constant maximum CPU performance. Appropriate use cases include small-scale machine learning inference, model prototyping, video transcoding, and moderately demanding graphics rendering tasks. The 550 GB NVMe SSD also supports data-intensive operations, making it viable for localized data processing and development environments.
